correctness.rationale: For an eigenpair, taking the imaginary part of the Rayleigh quotient gives Im λ=−γ|ψ_c|²/(2‖ψ‖²). Thus a real eigenmode has a node at the center; neither half can vanish because the center equation and the nonzero endpoint coupling would force the other half to vanish by recurrence. Reflect the clean right half to the standard Dirichlet basis. Its energy must be some simple E_k with normalized vector v_k. The rank-one determinant evaluated at E_k on the left equals −ε|v_k(s)|² times the nonzero product of all clean eigenvalue gaps. Thus ε≠0 permits precisely (m+1)|sk and the clean odd vector is unchanged there. The node count is gcd(m+1,s)−1. The nodal real eigenspaces are reducing, since for their vectors the adjoint has the same eigenvalue; no Jordan chain can meet them. In particular the dark E_k are simple at ε=0 (equivalently the even block is invertible at E_k by endpoint projection), so analytic normalized eigenvectors and eigenvalues exist locally. An independent coefficient derivation differentiates the full eigenvector equation. With left/right clean amplitudes v_k/√2 and −v_k/√2, λ'_k(0)=v_k(s)²/2 by the clean left eigenvector. Projection of the derivative equation on the reflected clean right v_k gives 0=J v_k(m)ψ'_c(0)+λ'_k(0)/√2. Substitution in the dissipation identity yields −γ v_k(s)^4/[16J²v_k(m)²] and hence the displayed sine coefficient. The decay rate for a mode's no-jump probability is −2 Im λ. Reflection gives the right-half case without changed normalization.
residual_risks: Fresh floating-point full-chain diagnostics checked 540 nonzero-detuning spectra (both signs) and 855 derivative coefficients, with maximum scaled coefficient error below 1.4×10⁻¹⁵. Tolerances are not exact multiplicity proofs; the determinant and dissipative argument justify strict spectral statements.

value.rationale: The exact combination distinguishes truly protected single-particle modes from branches that only appear dark at first order and supplies measurable leading lifetimes at arbitrary fixed loss. The arithmetic position dependence and a sine-fourth-power width divided by the endpoint weight are not implied by knowing the symmetry or a generic perturbative order. They are useful for tuning or diagnosing a single-site perturbation of a central-loss chain within the stated regime.
residual_risks: The value claim is confined to one-particle no-jump decay; it does not extend to driven steady states or many-body mixing.
